That said, haven't there been a lot more police officer deaths perpetrated by criminals, both on the streets and during arrests than criminal deaths by police? Have there been any criminal deaths that weren't justified? Again, I don't support violence, but who is being victimized?
explanation: This flips the original's implicit critique of ICE enforcement to a right-leaning critique that questions police accountability narratives. It maintains the same rhetorical structure of disclaiming violence while questioning victimization narratives, but shifts from defending migrants against ICE to defending police against what conservatives view as unfair characterization. The tone remains identical - appearing measured while making a pointed political argument through leading questions.

original_text: If we stop using fossil fuels, all the companies that are deeply invested in them will vanish almost overnight. They’re fighting hard to prevent that, aren’t they.
flipped_text: If we transition to green energy, all these renewable companies that Democrats are heavily invested in will make billions overnight. They're pushing this climate agenda hard to cash in, aren't they.
explanation: The flipped text maintains the same conspiratorial tone and rhetorical structure as the original, but shifts from a left-leaning critique of fossil fuel companies resisting change to a right-leaning critique of Democrats and renewable energy companies profiting from climate policies. Both versions use the same pattern of suggesting financial motivations behind political positions, ending with the same rhetorical question format that implies obvious corruption or self-interest.
